venues.name: Hotel Bel-Air, Dorchester Collection
venues.note: A twelve-acre canyon hideaway of swan lakes and secret gardens, Los Angeles at its most private.
credentials: World's 50 Best Hotels 2025 (No. 42, highest-ranked US hotel outside New York)

venues.name: The Beverly Hills Hotel, Dorchester Collection
venues.note: The Pink Palace on Sunset since 1912, the definitive myth of Beverly Hills, still gracious.

venues.name: Waldorf Astoria Beverly Hills
venues.note: A gleaming Pierre-Yves Rochon tower at Wilshire and Santa Monica, the marque's West Coast debut.

venues.name: The Peninsula Beverly Hills
venues.note: The group's flawless Californian house, the only Forbes Five-Star, AAA Five-Diamond hotel in Southern California, year after year.

venues.name: The Maybourne Beverly Hills
venues.note: The London group's Californian address, Claridge's polish, a block from Rodeo Drive.

venues.name: Beverly Wilshire, Beverly Hills, A Four Seasons Hotel
venues.note: A 1928 landmark at the foot of Rodeo Drive, grand-hotel bones, Four Seasons hands.

venues.name: Four Seasons Hotel Los Angeles at Beverly Hills
venues.note: The surest hands in Los Angeles, a leafy, low-key garden hotel on Doheny Drive.

venues.name: L'Ermitage Beverly Hills
venues.note: The longest-tenured all-suite Forbes Five-Star hotel in the world, discreet, residential calm.

venues.name: Nobu Ryokan Malibu
venues.note: A sixteen-room teak ryokan on Billionaire's Beach, the ocean at the foot of the bed.
credentials: Travel + Leisure, No. 1 Resort Hotel in the Continental US (World's Best)

venues.name: Chateau Marmont
venues.note: The most storied hotel in Hollywood, a Loire-château fantasy above the Sunset Strip.

venues.name: Pendry West Hollywood
venues.note: A sleek Sunset Strip tower with a rooftop over the whole city, contemporary and buzzing.

venues.name: The West Hollywood EDITION
venues.note: Ian Schrager's white, garden-wrapped tower, quiet-luxury calm with a rooftop and a basement club.

venues.name: Sunset Tower Hotel
venues.note: An Art Deco icon of the Sunset Strip, old-Hollywood glamour, discreetly kept alive.

venues.name: Shutters on the Beach
venues.note: A Cape-Cod beach house right on the sand, the ocean-side heart of Santa Monica.

venues.name: Hotel Casa del Mar
venues.note: A restored 1920s beach club on the sand, a grander, more romantic Santa Monica landmark.

venues.name: Fairmont Miramar Hotel & Bungalows
venues.note: A palm-shaded estate above the ocean bluffs, private bungalows and a century of history.

venues.name: The Georgian Hotel
venues.note: A turquoise Art Deco jewel newly reborn on Ocean Avenue, glamour with an ocean view.

venues.name: Santa Monica Proper Hotel
venues.note: Kelly Wearstler's sun-bleached, texture-rich design hotel a block from the beach.

venues.name: Downtown L.A. Proper Hotel
venues.note: A 1920s landmark reborn as Kelly Wearstler's living museum, the coolest room downtown.

venues.name: The Aster
venues.note: A members'-club hotel in the heart of Hollywood, a rooftop pool and a fashionable crowd.

venues.name: The Prospect Hollywood
venues.note: An intimate, design-forward hideaway in the hills above Hollywood, small and personal.

venues.name: The Paramour Estate
venues.note: A hilltop 1920s mansion turned private hotel, a Mediterranean villa above the city.

venues.name: Palihouse West Hollywood
venues.note: A residential-style boutique house on a quiet WeHo street, apartment-living ease.

venues.name: The Charlie
venues.note: A cluster of English-cottage bungalows once home to Charlie Chaplin's circle, private and green.

venues.name: Providence
venues.note: Michael Cimarusti's temple to seafood, Los Angeles's most decorated table, newly at three stars.

venues.name: Somni
venues.note: Aitor Zabala's intimate fourteen-seat counter, the first three-star ever awarded in LA County.

venues.name: n/naka
venues.note: Niki Nakayama's modern kaiseki, the most quietly revered tasting menu in Los Angeles.

venues.name: Hayato
venues.note: Brandon Go's eight-seat kaiseki hidden in the Arts District, Kyoto exactitude in Los Angeles.

venues.name: Mélisse
venues.note: Josiah Citrin's long-held two-star, contemporary French of great polish, on the Westside.

venues.name: Kato
venues.note: Jon Yao's Taiwanese-American tasting menu, personal, precise, and among the city's very best.

venues.name: Osteria Mozza
venues.note: Nancy Silverton's Italian benchmark, the mozzarella bar and pasta that set the LA standard.

venues.name: CUT by Wolfgang Puck
venues.note: The most glamorous steakhouse in America, Wolfgang Puck's starred room in the Beverly Wilshire.

venues.name: Orsa & Winston
venues.note: Josef Centeno's intimate Italian-Japanese tasting counter, a quiet downtown gem.

venues.name: Restaurant Ki
venues.note: A ten-seat contemporary Korean counter, global technique on a Korean foundation.

venues.name: Meteora
venues.note: Jordan Kahn's fire-driven, live-flame cooking, theatrical, primal, singular.

venues.name: Kali
venues.note: Kevin Meehan's seasonal Californian cooking, refined, ingredient-led, unshowy.

venues.name: Mori Nozomi
venues.note: An eight-seat sushi counter with fish flown from Japan multiple times a week, newly starred.

venues.name: Nozawa Bar
venues.note: A hidden ten-seat omakase behind Sugarfish, pure, classic edomae sushi.

venues.name: Shin Sushi
venues.note: A Valley omakase counter of great purity, quiet mastery away from the Westside crowds.

venues.name: Sushi Kaneyoshi
venues.note: A basement counter of exacting edomae sushi, a serious, hushed omakase downtown.

venues.name: Kojima
venues.note: An intimate sushi counter on Sawtelle's Japantown strip, refined and personal.

venues.name: Miura
venues.note: A precise Japanese counter that earned its star with quiet, seasonal craft.

venues.name: Pasta | Bar
venues.note: An intimate Italian tasting counter in the Valley, pasta as a tasting menu.

venues.name: Holbox
venues.note: Gilberto Cetina's Yucatán seafood counter, ceviches and tostadas good enough for a star.

venues.name: Vespertine
venues.note: Jordan Kahn's futuristic tasting menu in a Gehry-adjacent glass tower, dining as art installation.

venues.name: Pijja Palace
venues.note: An Indian-American sports bar that became LA's most loved crossover, tandoori spaghetti and cricket on the screens.

venues.name: Jitlada
venues.note: The fiery southern-Thai institution of LA's Thai Town, decades deep and still unrivalled.

venues.name: Pine & Crane
venues.note: Bright, modern Taiwanese home cooking in an airy room, fresh, fast, beloved.

venues.name: Pizzeria Bianco
venues.note: Chris Bianco's LA outpost, widely called the best pizza in America, now downtown.

venues.name: Pizzeria Mozza
venues.note: Nancy Silverton and Mario Batali's blistered-crust pizzas, the room that reset LA pizza.

venues.name: Pizzana
venues.note: Daniele Uditi's neo-Neapolitan pizza, soft, charred, and quietly perfect.

venues.name: Rossoblu
venues.note: Steve Samson's Bolognese cooking, handmade pasta and a warm, cavernous downtown room.

venues.name: Cobi's
venues.note: Bright, inventive Southeast-Asian cooking in a leafy garden room, fresh and easy to love.

venues.name: Colapasta
venues.note: A small, sincere pasta room doing handmade Italian classics on the Westside.

venues.name: Sea Harbour Seafood Restaurant
venues.note: Cantonese dim sum of real refinement, a San Gabriel Valley institution, fairly priced.

venues.name: The Getty Center
venues.note: Richard Meier's travertine acropolis above the city, a world-class art collection, gardens and the view, all free.

venues.name: Griffith Observatory
venues.note: The city's balcony to the stars, Art Deco domes, the planetarium, and the finest view of Los Angeles and the Hollywood Sign.

venues.name: The Getty Villa
venues.note: A Roman country house recreated above the Pacific, Greek and Roman antiquities in a garden of fountains.

venues.name: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA)
venues.note: The largest art museum in the western United States, and Chris Burden's Urban Light, the city's most photographed lamps.

venues.name: Walt Disney Concert Hall
venues.note: Frank Gehry's billowing steel masterpiece, home of the LA Philharmonic and the icon of downtown.

venues.name: The Broad
venues.note: A honeycomb-veiled museum of contemporary art, Koons, Warhol and Kusama's Infinity Mirror Rooms.

venues.name: The Huntington
venues.note: A railway magnate's estate of libraries, art and 120 acres of botanical gardens, a Gutenberg Bible among the roses.

venues.name: Santa Monica Pier & Beach
venues.note: The end of Route 66 over the Pacific, the Ferris wheel, the sand, and the quintessential Californian sunset.

venues.name: Hollywood, Walk of Fame, Chinese Theatre & the Sign
venues.note: The centre of the movie myth, the terrazzo stars, the handprints at Grauman's, and the Sign on the hill above.

venues.name: Rodeo Drive
venues.note: The most famous luxury shopping street in the world, the flagships of every great house, in three gilded blocks.

venues.name: The Academy Museum of Motion Pictures
venues.note: The definitive museum of cinema, in a Renzo Piano sphere, the art and machinery of the movies.

venues.name: The Broad Stage & Bergamot / Venice Canals & Boardwalk
venues.note: The bohemian edge of the city, the canals Abbot Kinney dug, the muscle-beach boardwalk, and Abbot Kinney's shops.

venues.name: Runyon Canyon & the Hollywood Hills trails
venues.note: The city's favourite hillside walk, a short, steep climb to a panorama of the whole basin.

venues.name: El Pueblo & Olvera Street
venues.note: The birthplace of Los Angeles, the oldest quarter of the city, and a lively Mexican marketplace.

venues.name: Mírate
venues.note: A rooftop mezcal-and-agave temple over Los Feliz, the highest-ranked bar in Los Angeles.
credentials: North America's 50 Best Bars 2025 (No. 12), highest LA entry

venues.name: Thunderbolt
venues.note: A breezy, boundary-pushing SoCal cocktail bar, laboratory technique with a Southern soul.

venues.name: Death & Co Los Angeles
venues.note: The New York cocktail institution's LA home, impeccable drinks in the Arts District.

venues.name: Genever
venues.note: A Filipina-run gin bar of real character, one of the city's most distinctive drinking rooms.

venues.name: Bar Next Door
venues.note: A speakeasy-style hideaway beneath a restaurant, intimate, low-lit, seriously made drinks.

venues.name: The Tower Bar, Sunset Tower Hotel
venues.note: Old-Hollywood glamour in Bugsy Siegel's former apartment, the most storied nightcap on the Strip.
credentials: Inside a MICHELIN One-Key hotel, a genuine Sunset Strip institution

venues.name: Bar Marmont / Chateau Marmont
venues.note: A drink in the most legendary hotel in Hollywood, discreet, dimly lit, endlessly mythologised.
credentials: Inside a MICHELIN Two-Key hotel, a Hollywood institution

venues.name: The Polo Lounge, The Beverly Hills Hotel
venues.note: The power-lunch and nightcap of Beverly Hills since 1941, pink banquettes under the tropical garden.
credentials: Inside a Forbes 5-Star, MICHELIN Three-Key hotel, a global institution

venues.name: Dante Beverly Hills, The Maybourne
venues.note: The New York World's-Best bar transplanted to a Maybourne rooftop, negronis with a view.
credentials: An outpost of a former World's Best Bar (Dante), atop a Forbes 5-Star hotel
